target_customer: Enterprises and building owners who want employees to open doors and use access systems from a phone, later consumers via a wearable wallet
problem: Keys, cards and badges were clumsy for physical access, payments and identity.
business_model: B2B hardware and software for access control integrations
product_category: mobile identity and access, wearable digital wallet

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed Bluetooth low energy identity signals, biometrics and integrations with legacy access control hardware and later wearable hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with installed access systems and a patent portfolio helped, but competitors like Kisi and Openpath addressed the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Access control incumbents added mobile credentials; Oura acquired Proxy in 2023 in an all-equity deal.

market_need_then: Physical credentials were widely used but costly to manage; smartphones and Bluetooth low energy made phone based access feasible.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no coverage about the brand itself; the name is generic and collides with proxy server businesses in search.

pivots.from: Stealth mobile wallet and Internet of things access idea
pivots.to: Proxy Signal universal identity for physical access
pivots.why: Emerged from stealth with an identity signal product per launch release

outcome_analysis: Proxy spent three years in stealth after YC, then raised a 13.6 million dollar Series A in 2019 and a 42 million dollar Series B in 2020 to sell Bluetooth phone based access to enterprises. It did not become independent at scale; Oura bought the team, patents and the Motiv ring brand in an all-equity deal in May 2023 to add payments and authentication to its smart ring. The exit price is not public.
notes: The directory lists no website and none was fetched, so the site is treated as gone after the acquisition. A 2016 report cites 2.1 million dollars raised while TechCrunch says 1.6 million. A seed of 2.6 million dollars on one aggregator is unverified. No dated 2016 competitor sources were found; Kisi, Openpath and Latch appear only in later comparison pages. Brand research found nothing specific.
